name: What is a kitchen work triangle and does it still matter?

mainEntity.name: What is a kitchen work triangle and does it still matter when changing a kitchen layout?
mainEntity.text: What is a kitchen work triangle and does it still matter when changing a kitchen layout?

acceptedAnswer.text: The work triangle is a classic layout concept that links the sink, stove, and refrigerator into an efficient path. It still matters because those three points remain core to most kitchens, but modern design often goes beyond that idea. Many homes now need separate prep, cleanup, cooking, storage, and coffee or beverage zones. Open layouts, larger kitchens, and multiple cooks can make a strict triangle less useful than a zone-based plan. The key is not to follow an old rule blindly, but to make sure the most important tasks can be completed without unnecessary steps or traffic conflicts. In practical terms, a good layout supports movement, storage, and safety while fitting the way the household actually cooks. The triangle is still a helpful guide, but it should be treated as one tool rather than the whole design strategy.
acceptedAnswer.description: The kitchen work triangle is the relationship between the sink, stove, and refrigerator. It still matters, but modern layouts often use broader work zones, multiple prep areas, and better circulation instead of relying on one strict triangle.
